summary: Same pattern family (tri-hue traveling stripes phase-shifted by a 1D noise field, same 11-dial surface, matching palette/stripe-count/weight behaviour), but the port's animation runs 13.6x-24x too slow (original color cycle 1.30 s, port 31.7 s untouched) and its noise field is EXACTLY mirror-symmetric about 1/6 of the strip in every frame, which the original never is.
observations: Rig: 60 px strip. Both sides bind sensor globals (wantsSensors true, fed beat120). Only the sliderBassThreshold path is audio-driven: with --sensors off both sides render identically to the fed run at default dials (jd-sensoff vs survey10: orig br 39.4 / motion 42.2 both, port br 28.5 / motion 1.6 both).

HEADLINE TIMING: original's whole-strip color cycle has period 1.30 s (meanR autocorrelation, lag 13 at 10 fps = 0.99, lag 26 = 0.95, lag 66 = 1.00, confirmed 1.30 s at 20 fps and 1.32 s at 40 fps). The port's period is 31.7 s (lag 317 at 10 fps = 1.00, 63.3 s = 1.00; 31.75 s at 20 fps, 32.13 s at 40 fps). Untouched ratio = 24.4x too slow. A time-rescale fit corr(orig[t], port[k*t]) over meanR/G/B on a 300 s run peaks at k = 24.75 (|corr| 0.64).

Two independent causes of that 24x, separated by dialing sliderStripeSpeed on both sides (jd-ss-*, 200 s @ 10 fps): (a) the port's UNTOUCHED default stripe speed equals its own sliderStripeSpeed=0.5 setting (both give period 31.70 s) while the original's untouched default equals its sliderStripeSpeed=1.0 setting (both 1.30 s) -- a factor of 2; (b) at MATCHED dial values the port is still far too slow: v=1 orig 1.30 s vs port 17.70 s (13.6x), v=0.5 orig 2.60 s vs port 31.70 s (12.2x), v=0.25 orig 5.30 s vs port 52.20 s (9.8x).

The original's period scales as exactly 1/v with sliderStripeSpeed (1.30 / 2.60 / 5.30 s at v = 1 / 0.5 / 0.25). The port's does not (17.70 / 31.70 / 52.20 s); its rate curve behaves like a linear-in-v term with a small constant offset, so the slowdown factor itself varies with the dial.

NOT frame-rate coupling in the base animation: both sides are fps-invariant. Rendering the same side at 10 / 20 / 40 fps gives orig 1.30 / 1.30 / 1.32 s and port 31.7 / 31.75 / 32.13 s. The port is genuinely slow, not frame-stepped.

STRUCTURE: the port's frame is EXACTLY mirror-symmetric (symmetry score 1.00, i.e. bit-for-bit palindromic brightness) about pixel 10 and pixel 40 on a 60 px strip, in every frame sampled at t = 0, 0.4, 0.8, 1.2, 9.9, 19.8, 29.7, 49.5, 74.3, 99 s, at default dials AND with sliderStripeSpeed/AutoColorPalette/BassThreshold explicitly set. The original never exceeds ~0.4 on the same metric (coincidental alignment only).

That mirror is resolution-independent, i.e. structural rather than a 60 px artefact: re-rendered at --pixels 120 the port's mirror centre is px 80, at --pixels 300 it is px 200 -- always 2/3 (equivalently 1/6) of the strip, score 1.00 in all cases. The original scores 0.24-0.44 at every rig size.

COLOR at untouched defaults: the original's palette is a triad at hues ~336 (magenta-red), ~96 (chartreuse), ~216 (azure) -- e.g. [239,0,95], [100,250,0], [0,88,220]. The port's untouched palette is the pure-primary triad 0 / 120 / 240 -- [236,0,0], [0,233,0], [0,0,252], never an intermediate hue. This is a default-value gap, not a palette-model gap: sliderAutoColorPalette rotates the triad as hue_offset = -360*v on BOTH sides identically, and setting sliderAutoColorPalette=0.4 on both makes the colours agree exactly (verified across 21 values 0.00-1.00 -- e.g. v=0.05 gives {342,102,222} on both, v=0.50 gives {60,180,300} on both, v=1 wraps back to {0,120,240} on both).

BRIGHTNESS: the port runs consistently dimmer at default dials -- meanBrightness 28.5 vs the original's 39.4 (about -28%), reproduced at every window length (6 s, 60 s, 300 s) and at 120 px and 300 px rigs (port 22 vs orig 40). Dialing sliderStripeWeight=1 on both closes some of it (39.4 vs 28.6) but the gap persists at every setting.

SPATIAL FEATURE DENSITY at default dials is comparable: 8-10 brightness peaks per frame on the port vs 8-9 on the original, and 4-9 hue segments vs 5-8. So the stripe count is roughly right; it is the phase field's symmetry and the speed that are wrong.

Waterfall character (jd-dialed, 20 s @ 10 fps, matched palette): the original draws ~30 crisp thin wavy bands stacked over the window -- a fast, lively churn -- while the port draws 1.5 broad chevrons over the same 20 s, reading as near-frozen vertical stripes at the default 6 s window (motion stat 24 vs 1 in baseline).

CONTROL-SURFACE NAME MISMATCHES (both sides expose 11 sliders, all probe-responsive): the original has 'sliderPerlinOrSimplex' where the port has 'sliderNoiseType', and the original has 'sliderX_Offset' where the port has 'sliderXOffset'. The other nine names match exactly (sliderScale, sliderMotion, sliderAutoColor, sliderAutoColorPalette, sliderNumberOfStripes, sliderStripeSpeed, sliderStripeWeight, sliderShowProgress, sliderBassThreshold), all kind 'slider' on both sides.

MODE-BOUNDARY OFF-BY-ONE on three two-mode sliders. Frame-hash sweeps at 0.01-0.05 resolution show the original switches strictly ABOVE 0.5 and the port switches AT 0.5: sliderPerlinOrSimplex/sliderNoiseType -- orig mode A at v<=0.50, mode B at v>=0.51; port mode A at v<=0.49, mode B at v>=0.50. Identical boundary offset on sliderAutoColor and sliderShowProgress. Consequence: at exactly v=0.5 (the natural midpoint a user lands on) the two sides are in DIFFERENT modes on three separate dials.

FRAME-RATE COUPLING IN THE PORT'S AUDIO PATH: at 20 fps both sides react to the beat at every sliderBassThreshold >= 0.1 (orig motion 23.9 -> 46.2; port 1 -> 27.7 at v=0.1, 18.9 for v >= 0.2). At 10 fps the port's reaction DIES for v >= 0.9 (motion 2, i.e. back to inert) while the original keeps reacting at full strength (motion 65) at every v. Reproduced at v=0.9 and v=1.0. The original's bass response is fps-independent; the port's is not.

No mode rotation or long-period regime structure on either side: a 300 s / 10 fps run shows one steady regime throughout on both, the original repeating every 1.30 s and the port every 31.7 s. brightnessTrend steady on both; no decay, no saturation, no freeze. Steady state at t=99 s looks like t=0 s on both sides.

Both sides are seed-independent: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 give byte-identical statsSummary on both sides (br 39.4/28.5, motion 42.2/1.6). The pattern is deterministic, so the randomness caveat does not apply.

dials.name: sliderPerlinOrSimplex (orig) / sliderNoiseType (port)
dials.origEffect: two-mode selector; switches to mode B strictly above v=0.5 (0.50 -> A, 0.51 -> B)
dials.portEffect: two-mode selector; switches at v=0.5 (0.49 -> A, 0.50 -> B). Also the control is RENAMED.

dials.name: sliderScale
dials.origEffect: spatial frequency: 4 -> 11 -> 14 brightness peaks per frame at v = 0 / 0.5 / 1
dials.portEffect: same direction but compressed range: 6 -> 8 -> 10 peaks. Never as coarse at v=0 nor as fine at v=1.

dials.name: sliderMotion
dials.origEffect: raises motion 42.1 -> 40.8 -> 45.4 at v = 0 / 0.5 / 1 and breaks the clean 1.30 s periodicity at v=1 (adds wander on top of the stripe travel)
dials.portEffect: same direction, motion 1.6 -> 1.8 -> 2.1, but ~20x smaller in absolute terms because the whole animation is 24x slow

dials.name: sliderAutoColor
dials.origEffect: two-mode; v<=0.5 gives br 33.6 with a fast 0.40 s color cycle, v=1 gives br 39.4 with the 1.30 s cycle
dials.portEffect: same two modes and same direction, but the boundary is at v=0.5 not above it, and the two modes' cycles are 10.4 s and >30 s (again ~24x slow)

dials.name: sliderAutoColorPalette
dials.origEffect: continuous hue rotation of the 3-hue triad, hue_offset = -360*v (v=0 -> {0,120,240}, v=0.05 -> {342,102,222}, v=0.5 -> {60,180,300}, v=1 wraps)
dials.portEffect: identical mapping at all 21 values swept; hues agree to within 1-3 degrees at every setting

dials.name: sliderNumberOfStripes
dials.origEffect: v=0 collapses the strip to a single hue segment (motion 41.7, aperiodic); v=0.5 gives 6-8 segments; v=1 gives 11-12 segments and br 41.7
dials.portEffect: v=0 also collapses to one hue segment; v=0.5 gives 4-9; v=1 gives 11-16 segments and br 42.7 -- same behaviour and comparable counts

dials.name: sliderStripeSpeed
dials.origEffect: v=0 freezes completely (motion 0); period scales exactly as 1/v: 5.30 s / 2.60 s / 1.30 s at v = 0.25 / 0.5 / 1
dials.portEffect: v=0 also freezes; but periods are 52.20 s / 31.70 s / 17.70 s -- 9.8x / 12.2x / 13.6x too slow, and the curve is not 1/v

dials.name: sliderStripeWeight
dials.origEffect: brightness ramp 7.9 -> 13.1 -> 39.4 at v = 0 / 0.5 / 1; low values leave only thin dim stripes
dials.portEffect: same ramp shape 5.5 -> 9.4 -> 28.6, consistently ~28% dimmer at every setting

dials.name: sliderX_Offset (orig) / sliderXOffset (port)
dials.origEffect: reshapes the noise field (not a pure translation): peak count stays 3-10, best circular-shift correlation against v=0 drops to 0.34-0.45
dials.portEffect: reshapes too, BUT at v=1 it explodes to 18 brightness peaks vs the original's 7, and the port regains near-perfect mirror symmetry (0.95). Also RENAMED.

dials.name: sliderShowProgress
dials.origEffect: two-mode; adds an overlay above v=0.5 (br 39.4 -> 41.3, motion 42.1 -> 46.3, +2 hue segments)
dials.portEffect: same overlay, same direction (br 28.6 -> 34.7, motion 1.6 -> 3.1), but the boundary is at v=0.5 not above it

dials.name: sliderBassThreshold
dials.origEffect: v=0 disables beat reactivity; any v>=0.1 enables it and the response is a flat plateau (motion 23.9 -> 46.2 at 20 fps, 0.60 s beat-locked cycle), identical at 10 and 20 fps
dials.portEffect: correct shape at 20 fps (motion 1 -> 27.7/18.9, plateau from v=0.1) but at 10 fps the reaction dies for v>=0.9 (motion back to 2) -- the port's audio path is frame-rate coupled

feedback: PRIMARY: the port's animation rate is 13.6x too slow at sliderStripeSpeed=1 and 24.4x too slow untouched. Original color cycle = 1.30 s; port = 17.70 s dialed / 31.7 s untouched. Target: at sliderStripeSpeed=1 the whole-strip color cycle must complete in 1.30 s, and the period must scale as exactly 1/sliderStripeSpeed (2.60 s at 0.5, 5.30 s at 0.25). The port's curve is currently not 1/v, so it is not just a scalar factor -- there is an extra constant term in its rate.

SECONDARY (part of the same gap): the port's UNTOUCHED default stripe speed is half the original's. Untouched, the port renders exactly what it renders at sliderStripeSpeed=0.5 (31.70 s), while the original untouched renders exactly what it renders at sliderStripeSpeed=1.0 (1.30 s). Raise the port's default so the untouched render matches the sliderStripeSpeed=1 render.

STRUCTURAL: the port's spatial field is EXACTLY mirror-symmetric about 1/6 (equivalently 2/3) of the strip -- brightness is bit-for-bit palindromic in every frame, at every rig size (60/120/300 px) and with dials set. The original is never symmetric. The port's noise coordinate is evidently an even/folding function of position (a triangle or absolute-value fold) where the original's is monotone. Fix the position-to-noise-coordinate mapping so it advances monotonically across the strip; that alone will kill the chevron/V waterfall look and restore the original's irregular travelling stripes.

DEFAULT PALETTE: untouched, the original's hue triad is {336, 96, 216} (magenta-red / chartreuse / azure) and the port's is {0, 120, 240} (pure red/green/blue). The palette DIAL itself is correct on both sides (hue_offset = -360*v, verified at 21 values), so this is purely a default -- set the port's default sliderAutoColorPalette-equivalent to the value that yields a -24 degree hue offset (dial value ~0.067, or equivalently 0.4 / 0.733).

MODE BOUNDARIES: three two-mode sliders switch one step early on the port. Original switches strictly ABOVE 0.5 (v=0.50 -> mode A, v=0.51 -> mode B); the port switches AT 0.5 (v=0.49 -> A, v=0.50 -> B). Affects sliderNoiseType, sliderAutoColor and sliderShowProgress. At the exact midpoint -- the value a user is most likely to land on -- all three dials put the two sides in different modes. Move the port's comparison to strictly-greater-than.

CONTROL NAMES: the port renames two controls. 'sliderPerlinOrSimplex' became 'sliderNoiseType' and 'sliderX_Offset' became 'sliderXOffset'. These names are user-visible in the UI and in the saved control state; restore the original spellings.

sliderX_Offset at v=1: the original draws 7 brightness peaks, the port draws 18 and snaps back into perfect mirror symmetry. The port's offset term is scaling the noise coordinate as well as translating it. Once the fold above is fixed, re-check that v=1 leaves feature count roughly unchanged (original stays in the 3-10 peak range across the whole dial).

sliderScale range is compressed on the port: at v=0 the original is coarser (4 peaks vs the port's 6) and at v=1 the original is finer (14 peaks vs the port's 10). Widen the port's scale mapping at both ends.
BRIGHTNESS: the port is ~28% dimmer than the original at every sliderStripeWeight setting (meanBrightness 28.5 vs 39.4 untouched; 28.6 vs 39.4 at weight=1). Same shape, wrong gain.

AUDIO PATH FRAME-RATE COUPLING: at 10 fps the port stops reacting to the beat entirely for sliderBassThreshold >= 0.9 (motion drops to 2) while the original reacts identically at 10 and 20 fps at every threshold. The port's beat detector or its envelope decay is counting frames rather than elapsed time. Verify with --fps 10 --controls-both sliderBassThreshold=1 after the fix: the port should post the same beat cadence it does at --fps 20.

Already correct, do not regress: sliderAutoColorPalette (exact hue match across the full range), sliderNumberOfStripes (v=0 collapses to one segment on both, v=1 gives 11-16 segments on both), sliderStripeWeight direction, sliderStripeSpeed=0 freezing both sides, seed-independence, and fps-invariance of the base animation.
